data.exact_reserve_text: Included within net claims incurred of GBP 473.6m (2019: GBP 302.5m) is a deterioration of GBP 7.9m (2019: deterioration of GBP 8.4m) to claims reserves established at the prior year end principally due to unfavourable developments on Property, Third party liability and Accident and Health with partially offsetting favourable developments across the other classes.

named_events.loss_description: Claims in respect of the Covid-19 pandemic total GBP 128m net of reinsurance recoveries, adding 27% to the net loss ratio.
The Syndicate's biggest exposure to these was through hurricane Laura (net incurred claims of GBP 21.5m).
Additionally, the Syndicate was exposed to Hurricanes Zeta and Sally
smaller US weather events including the Midwest Derecho storm
several instances of tornadoes and hail storms.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year reserve strengthening of GBP 7.9 million in 2020, representing 1.73% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This adverse development was primarily driven by unfavourable developments on Property, Third Party Liability, and Accident & Health classes, partially offset by favourable developments in other classes. The overall results for the year were significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and a record-breaking hurricane season, including Hurricane Laura, Zeta, Sally, and the Midwest Derecho storm. The 2018 year of account also closed with a reported net loss of GBP 55.7 million, and the 2019 prior year end experienced a deterioration of GBP 8.4 million.
raw_causal_phrases: unfavourable developments on Property, Third party liability and Accident and Health
partially offsetting favourable developments across the other classes
enormous financial impact of both the Covid-19 pandemic and a record breaking hurricane season
Claims in respect of the Covid-19 pandemic total GBP 128m net of reinsurance recoveries

The discontinued Contingency class, written on the 2018 and 2019 years of account, was the most severely impacted line as a result of the large number of event cancellations following the restrictions imposed in an effort to contain the virus.

Other classes were also impacted, to a lesser extent, as a result of business interruption (UK Property and Treaty Property classes), the recessionary impacts of the pandemic following the sharp decline in economic activity (Casualty, Political Risk and Treaty classes) as well as from an increase in medical expenses and travel related claims (Accident and Health).
Catastrophe experience in the year was heavier than expectation
Significant losses relating to Covid-19 have been felt across multiple classes
significant aggregate losses from natural catastrophes
data.data_quality_notes: The gross claims development triangle is distorted by a Reinsurance to Close (RITC) transaction for the 2017 year of account into the 2018 year of account, making it unreliable for calculating prior year development.
